name: TPS92200D1DDCR
title: TPS92200: 4 V to 30 V in, 1.5 A synchronous buck LED driver with PWM or analog dimming
summary: A synchronous buck converter built to drive a string of LEDs at a set current up to 1.5 A from 4 V to 30 V. Both power switches are inside (150 mΩ high side, 90 mΩ low side), it runs at 1 MHz with peak-current-mode control and internal compensation, and LED current is set by a sense resistor against a 99 mV feedback reference. One DIM pin enables the part and dims it: the D1 version accepts a logic PWM signal or a 0.65 V to 1.2 V analog voltage, the D2 version converts a 20 kHz to 200 kHz PWM duty into an analog reference for 1 % to 100 % dimming. It protects against open and shorted LEDs, a shorted or open sense resistor and overtemperature, mostly by auto-retry, and comes in a 6-pin SOT-23-THIN or a 1.5 × 2 mm VQFN-HR.

circuits.title: TPS92200D1 12-V input, 1.5-A, 2-piece IR LED driver with analog dimming
circuits.description: A buck stage running from 10.8 V to 13.2 V that pushes up to 1.5 A through two series IR LEDs. The LED string sits between the output and FB, and the 66 mΩ resistor from FB to ground sets the current against the 99 mV reference. A voltage of 0.65 V to 1.2 V on DIM scales the current down to about 5 % of full. C2 and C3 bypass the input, C4 smooths the LED ripple, and C1 feeds the high-side gate driver.

operation.text: Peak-current-mode buck with compensation inside the chip. The FB voltage across the sense resistor goes to an error amplifier against VREF; its output sets the peak current of the high-side switch, with slope compensation added against sub-harmonic oscillation at high duty. When the sensed peak reaches the amplifier output the high-side switch turns off and the low-side switch conducts for the rest of the cycle. The switching frequency is set inside the part to 1 MHz while the minimum off-time is not reached.
A resistor from the bottom of the LED string to ground sets the current: RSENSE = 99 mV / ILED.
VREF ramps up over the internal soft-start time, 0.5 ms typical.
The part stops when IN drops below about 3.5 V and has about 0.2 V of hysteresis.
A regulator inside charges the capacitor between BOOT and SW, which supplies the high-side gate drive. A 0.1 µF X7R or X5R ceramic is the recommended part.
When the input comes close to the output voltage the part lowers its switching frequency so the on-time can stretch up to tMAX_ON, 6.6 µs typical, which lifts the maximum duty cycle to about 99 %.

A clamp on the current command turns the high-side switch off at ILIM_HS in every cycle. If the overcurrent lasts longer than 512 switching cycles, the part shuts off for 60 ms typical and then tries again.

The low-side current is checked at the end of every cycle. If it is above ILIM_LS_SOUR, the high-side switch skips the next cycle and the low-side switch stays on, until a new cycle opens with the current under that limit.

Reverse current in the low-side switch is sensed from the voltage across it; at ILIM_LS_SINK both switches turn off, and the high side is allowed on again when a cycle begins with the current back below that limit.
With no LED current, FB sits near zero, the error amplifier saturates high and the high-side switch runs at maximum duty.

FB rises above VREF, the amplifier output clamps low and the high-side switch runs at minimum on-time. With too little output voltage the inductor current can climb until the low-side sourcing limit (3 A typical) holds it. Once FB passes VFB_OVP the auto-retry timer runs: after tRETRY_ON both switches go off for tRETRY_OFF, then the part restarts, repeating until the short is gone. The overcurrent limits stay active throughout.

FB is low, the amplifier output clamps high and the high-side switch runs at maximum duty; when either current limit trips, the auto-retry cycle of tRETRY_ON then tRETRY_OFF with both switches off begins and repeats until the short is removed.

FB rises above VREF and the high-side switch runs at minimum on-time; above VFB_OVP the auto-retry cycle starts. A separate 1 V comparator on FB switches both FETs off at once and starts tRETRY_OFF, which keeps FB from being overstressed during tRETRY_ON.
FB is low and the amplifier output clamps high; once either switch hits its current limit, auto-retry begins and repeats until the fault clears.
If more than 1 V appears on FB, both switches turn off immediately and the part waits tRETRY_OFF before restarting; it keeps cycling while the fault remains.

The part shuts down when the junction reaches 160 °C typical and restarts once it has cooled to 145 °C typical. The thermal shutdown threshold is also specified as 165 °C typical with 15 °C hysteresis.

DIM doubles as the enable. With VIN above UVLO, holding DIM above VDIM_H for longer than tDIM_ON1 turns the part on; holding it below VDIM_L for longer than tDIM_OFF turns it off. DIM is high impedance, so a pulldown resistor is needed for the part to default to off.

A logic signal on DIM, high above 1.4 V and low below 0.3 V (outside the 0.65 V to 1.2 V analog window), puts the D1 into PWM dimming: the output follows the input high and low. A frequency of 100 Hz to 2 kHz gives good dimming accuracy. Output duty equals input duty from 0 % to 100 %.
A steady voltage between 0.65 V and 1.2 V on DIM scales VREF linearly, from 5 mV at 0.65 V to 99 mV at 1.2 V.
On the D2, the duty cycle of a logic signal on DIM sets VREF linearly, from 0 mV at 0 % duty to 99 mV at 100 % duty. The signal must be between 20 kHz and 200 kHz.

The inductor's RMS and saturation current ratings must exceed what the application sees. Start-up, transients and faults can push inductor current above normal, so the safest choice saturates no lower than the current limit, though size may not allow it.

X5R or X7R ceramics are recommended for low ESR and small temperature drift. A 10 µF capacitor plus a 0.1 µF from VIN to GND suits most designs; the voltage rating must exceed the highest input voltage. The supply feeding IN, 4 V to 30 V, should be well regulated.

The output capacitor shunts high-frequency ripple away from the LED string; more ripple raises the string's RMS current and so its temperature. Size it from the string's dynamic resistance, the allowed LED ripple and the inductor ripple, then add for DC-bias derating.

Use a large ground plane for electrical and thermal performance, and make IN and GND traces wide, which also spreads heat. Thermal vias can tie the top ground to inner layers. Place the input capacitors right at IN and GND. Keep the SW trace short to limit radiated noise, and keep switching current from flowing beneath the part. Keep the FB trace short and away from the SW trace and from the ground shield. At higher currents, the sense-resistor return may need to run to the point where the input capacitor meets GND.
